$description: My First Bitcoin brand tokens (W3C Design Token Community Group format). Canonical source of truth: Figma 'My First Bitcoin_Full Brand Assets' (file mFIc75UUSyftaqnNUQgjLX). This file is the code-side mirror of the Figma variables; edit it ONLY to match Figma, never the other way around.

purple-300.$description: Primary purple: the main brand color for surfaces and shapes (backgrounds, covers, parallelograms, spotlights). Takes white text. Not a heading color on light backgrounds: headings there are black (Type Relationships 918:2990)

purple-400.$description: Accent dark purple — deep contrast, footer backgrounds

purple-200.$description: Accent light purple: supergraphic shapes on purple-300 (one step lighter than the base, 918:3604), halftone cutout backgrounds (918:3730). Takes white text

orange-300.$description: Primary orange: CTA and shape fills with black text (Color Contrast 918:2588), the highlighter line, the Bitcoin symbol, links on dark backgrounds. Never text on light backgrounds

orange-400.$description: Accent dark orange: hover and active fills, shapes; takes black text (918:2616). Never text on light backgrounds

orange-200.$description: Accent light orange: supergraphic shapes on orange-300 (one step lighter than the base, 918:3604), soft accents on dark backgrounds. Takes black text

black.$description: Primary black: headings and body text on light backgrounds and on orange (Type Relationships 918:2990, Color Contrast 918:2588)

white.$description: Primary white — backgrounds, text on dark surfaces

gray-900.$description: Neutral: the darkest grey, a dark surface that takes white text (918:2588). Text on light backgrounds is black, not gray-900 (918:2990)

gray-800.$description: Neutral: a dark grey surface that takes white text (918:2588)

gray-600.$description: Neutral: borders and dividers. As text, large sizes only (3.5:1 on white); as a surface it takes white text at large sizes (918:2588)

angle-base.$description: Brand slant, as a MAGNITUDE. The parent skew is negative and the counter-skew on child content is positive: skewX(calc(-1 * var(--sg-angle-base))) on the container, skewX(var(--sg-angle-base)) on the content inside it, or the text comes out slanted. So -13deg in a stylesheet is CORRECT, and the value to be suspicious of is any magnitude that is not 13. Stated here because a reader given only "13deg" cannot tell which sign the transform wants, and that ambiguity is the one this whole token set exists to remove.

mfb.note: Read through the Figma MCP (read only). The base parallelogram 918:4200 runs 44.01 over 190.63 (13.00deg from vertical); the logo icon inside instance 918:2708 runs 35.002 over 151.61 (13.00deg); the photo frames 918:4140, 918:4150, 918:4156, 918:4162 and 918:4208 measure 13.01 to 13.02deg. Also stated as prose at 918:4219 (Patterns slide) and 918:3789 ('Both cuts use a 13deg angle'). Parallelograms and the logo icon measure from vertical; the book panel's cuts (918:3777) measure from horizontal. The decorative slivers drawn at 13.71deg (918:4298 and others) are book-internal drift. The only machine-readable -13deg rotation in the file is a misuse example (918:2783, 'Don't place the logo on an angle'). Until 2026-10-06 this cited 918:4196, a node inside a hidden frame, as prose.

angle-alt.$description: Spotlight second cut. Must differ from angle-base.

mfb.note: Not in the brand book: node 918:3637 says only 'two diagonal cuts with different angles' and names no number. The nearest drawn construction line (918:3645) measures -21.9deg. A maintainer decision on 2026-08-19: keep 24deg and record it as declared rather than invent provenance. On the list of what Figma owes.

logo-icon-h.$description: Brand base unit. Height of the logo icon.

mfb.note: Not in the Brand Book: 918:4196 (inside a hidden frame) states no pixel value. The book's minimum logo size is 120px wide and 63px tall (logo.min-width, logo.min-height); a 40px tall logo is about 76px wide, below it. The canon draws .sg-logo and .sg-cover__logo at this height. Kept as the supergraphics base unit until it is decided. Until 2026-10-06 this cited figma:918:4196 as prose.

base-h-ratio.$description: Parallelogram base height as a multiple of the logo icon height.

mfb.note: Brand Book: 'The base parallelogram height equals 2× the height of the logo icon.' (the visible copy, 918:4219 on the Patterns slide 918:4212; the copy at 918:4196 sits in a hidden frame). No drawing in the book shows the 2x relation: 918:4200 is drawn at 1.00x the icon of 918:4199, and the Brand in Use slivers are 4.6x and 5.5x the logo height (918:4177 against 918:4186, 918:3820 against 918:3827). The prose stays normative. Until 2026-10-06 this cited 918:4196.

aspect.$description: Default supergraphic container aspect ratio, width over height.

halftone-highlight.$description: Halftone highlight cap. NOT a palette token.

mfb.note: supergraphics.css:270-274 warns these are book-specified standalone values and must NOT be 'corrected' to purple-200/purple-400. Kept out of the palette deliberately. Brand Book Halftones slide, text node 918:3737: 'Cutout portraits: Highlights #F7E6FF, Shadows #45265B'. The source was figma:918:4126 until 2026-10-06; that node is the Parallelogram Frames slide, which has no halftone text.

halftone-highlight-full.$description: Halftone highlight cap for full portraits (the subject fills the frame). Cutout portraits use halftone-highlight. NOT a palette token.

mfb.note: Brand Book Halftones slide, text node 918:3737, on two lines: 'Cutout portraits: Highlights #F7E6FF, Shadows #45265B' and 'Full portraits: Highlights #EEEEEE, Shadows #45265B'. Read through the Figma MCP on 2026-10-06. The shadow is the same halftone-shadow for both. Kept out of the palette, like halftone-highlight.

halftone-shadow.$description: Halftone shadow underlay and dot grid. NOT a palette token.

mfb.note: See halftone-highlight. Do not fold into the palette. Brand Book Halftones slide, text node 918:3737, gives Shadows #45265B for both cutout and full portraits. The source was figma:918:4126 (the Parallelogram Frames slide) until 2026-10-06.

highlighter-coverage.$description: Share of the word's width the highlighter line covers, centred, so it starts a little in from the first letter (10%) and stops short of the last (90%).

mfb.note: Brand Book Highlighter slide, text node 918:2878: 'Apply it to only one word per heading, covering up to 80% of the word length. Do not alter its appearance to ensure a clean and cohesive typographic style.' Measured on the same slide (Highlighter slide 918:2874, lines 918:2883 (on purple-300), 918:2887 (on orange-300), 918:2893 (on grey), 918:2898 (on white)): 79.8%, 82.5% and 82.7% of the ink width, 77.0% to 81.1% of the advance width, starting 8.1% to 9.4% in from the left ink edge. Brand in Use (918:3514, 918:4458) departs from this (70% to 88%); the slide is treated as normative.

highlighter-aspect.$description: Highlighter line length over its thickness (bounding height). The Brand Book draws the thickness in proportion to the line's length, so to the word's width, not as a share of the font size: at 80% coverage the line is about 3% of the word's width thick.

mfb.note: Measured from the vector geometry through the Figma MCP (read only). 26.6 on 918:2883 and 918:2898 (Education, the same geometry), 26.2 on 918:2887 (convince), 27.7 on 918:2893 (Unconference); 28.1 to 29.3 in Brand in Use. A fixed em thickness would read too thin under long words (Unconference is 0.187em).

highlighter-offset.$description: Distance from the text baseline down to the centre of the highlighter line's bounding box (half-way between its top and bottom edges), which is the point the CSS positions. The line straddles the baseline and sits mostly below it, behind the glyphs.

mfb.note: Measured through the Figma MCP (read only) on 2026-10-06, from node positions and IBM Plex Sans metrics (baseline 0.875em below the top of a line at 100% line height). On 918:2883 (Education, 48px, second line of text node 918:2884) the vector's box runs from 210.39 to 216.79 and the baseline is at 211.00, so the box centre is 2.59px (0.054em) below it; a raster of the slide puts that baseline at the same place. 918:2898 (the same Education on white) gives 0.054em; 918:2893 (Unconference, 48px) 0.036em; 918:2887 (convince, assuming its quote is set at 40px with 100% line height) 0.0375em. Follows the cited source node, as highlighter-aspect does. Replaces 0.03em, which measured to the shape's average centreline rather than to its box centre.

highlighter-shape.$description: Outline of the highlighter line in its bounding box, as a CSS clip-path: a filled quad that tapers from 6/7 of the box height at the start to 4/7 at the end, rises slightly to the right and has slant-cut ends.

mfb.note: All 12 highlighters in the Brand Book are one vector ('Vector 384') copied and scaled, drawn beneath the text in layer order. Corners taken from the SVG paths of 918:2883, 918:2887, 918:2893, 918:2898, 918:3518, 918:3574, 918:4475, 918:4501 and 918:4509. Variants: 918:3537 and 918:3559 put the top-left x at 0.71%; 918:4463 has y fractions 0.20 and 0.53.

para-edge-ratio.$description: Horizontal edge of the base parallelogram as a multiple of its height: the logo icon's own proportions. Pattern pieces may vary in width; the base shape does not.

mfb.note: Read through the Figma MCP (read only). 918:4200: edge 109.01 over height 190.63 = 0.5718; the logo icon's edge 86.70 over 151.61 = 0.5718. Pattern pieces vary (0.3415 on the rows of 918:4295), so width is free in patterns.

pattern-row-step.$description: Height ratio between adjacent rows of a progressive parallelogram pattern.

mfb.note: Read through the Figma MCP (read only). Rows 918:4297 164.62, 918:4371 197.54, 918:4402 237.05, 918:4348 197.54, 918:4323 164.62: exactly 1.2000 per step. Paired accent slivers are also 1.2 apart (918:4135 and 918:4136, 918:4146 and 918:4147, 918:4177 and 918:4182, 918:3820 and 918:3822). The prose (918:4222) says only 'subtle and consistent'; the purple panel 918:4228 steps 1.254. The canon's .sg-para-pattern--progressive uses 1.25 and 1.55 and does not read this token yet.

pattern-row-gap.$description: Vertical gap between the rows of a parallelogram pattern: the rows touch.

mfb.note: Read through the Figma MCP (read only). Row edges 84.62 and 84.78, 282.32 and 282.48, 519.52 and 519.11, 716.65 and 716.82 on 918:4295; 81.71 and 81.29, 163 and 163, 228.17 and 227.83 on 918:4228. The canon's .sg-para-pattern uses a 10px gap and does not read this token yet.

$verification: Colour and the IBM Plex Sans families, sizes and weights are checked against Figma page 262:2 by scripts/verify-figma.mjs, which counts rendered solid fills and text styles. That is the ONLY machine-checkable provenance in this file. Every token carries $extensions.mfb.sourceKind: rendered-fill or rendered-text (checkable), prose (stated in the Brand Book as English, a human transcribed it, unverifiable by machine), measured (read off the Brand Book's vector geometry or a node's rendered fill, by hand or by an AI session through the Figma MCP, with the node ids in the note; no machine re-checks it), declared (not in the Brand Book), or unverified (provenance never established). The source rule: where the Brand Book defines a value, it wins. Where it is silent, a value may be declared from the live website, which was built following the Brand Book: sourceKind declared, source myfirstbitcoin.org@<commit>, <CSS name>: a commit on the site's main branch and the CSS that carries the value in what the site serves (a custom property, a selector and property, or a property set inline, with where it is used). The site's source repository is private, so no file or line of it is named here; the deciders named in CONTRIBUTING keep the exact lines outside this repository. A website value that contradicts the Brand Book is never declared. Any other declared value has source declared and says in its note why it exists. Colour roles (colorRole) and shape tones (shapeTone) are aliases of palette colours, and the build refuses one that is not. Geometry added 2026-08-19: it had never been in the pipeline, which is why five different slant angles reached production.
